claims.detail: SBIC East Japan's official profile names the company Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. (SBIC East Japan), established in 1963, with 96 employees, ¥6.6734B capital and an 18-prefecture operating area.

The Japanese company describes itself as an independent private corporation and policy-implementing institution established under the 1963 Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Companies Act; it is not SBI Holdings.
The original 2019 paper defines SBIC as Social Bias Inference Corpus and describes 44,671 social-media posts with approximately 150,000 structured annotations.

A 2024 paper explicitly evaluates ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) on the SBIC dataset, using a 4,000-item training sample and a 1,000-item test sample; the paper reports 68.5% accuracy and 72.82 F1 for its ChatGPT CoT baseline, with higher results for its distilled method.

The exact phrase 'ChatGPT SBIC' has a verified academic use referring to ChatGPT evaluated on the Social Bias Inference Corpus. This is the strongest located match for that phrase, but does not prove it is the user's intended context.

Permission's official tokenomics documentation describes ASK as its native token and claims it supports family rewards, permissioned participation, agent-to-agent value exchange, and future governance/staking.

Permission's official contract page lists ASK as a LayerZero OFT-20 on Base and Polygon, with official contracts 0xBB146326778227A8498b105a18f84E0987A684b4 and 0xaA3717090CDDc9B227e49d0D84A28aC0a996e6Ff, and states that Stargate support is live.

Permission's tokenomics page says a portion of parent subscription revenue is used to buy ASK on the open market and that purchased ASK funds rewards. No transaction-level buyback evidence or audited cash-flow reconciliation was established in this pass.

Permission's January 10, 2025 blog says ASK launched on Base and could be swapped through Coinbase Wallet. This supports a wallet-interface route on Base, not a Coinbase exchange listing, Coinbase investment, custody relationship or endorsement.

Permission's official contract page lists Base and Polygon only; searches within its tokenomics and contract documentation returned no XRP or Ripple reference. No XRP Ledger deployment or direct XRP relationship was established.

The exact phrase 'actual capital' did not resolve to a verified XRP-specific entity, project, filing or transaction in this search pass. It may describe a general capital-flow concept rather than a proper name.

Searches for an exact-name Camilla Stephenson YouTube channel or videos, including XRP/ASK/SBIC terms, did not surface a verifiable channel or video. Direct YouTube search results were not reliably readable; this is not proof that no such videos exist.
Permission Coin (ASK) is a plausible ticker match for 'ASK Coin', but no evidence confirms that this is the user's intended ASK asset; other unrelated ASK tickers or projects may exist.

No direct Permission-Coin relationship to Ripple, XRP, Circle, SBI/SBIC or Coinbase as a corporate counterparty was established. The only Coinbase-adjacent evidence found is Permission's statement that ASK could be swapped through Coinbase Wallet on Base.
